raw_source.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 25\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 25\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=19 \\ y+2z &=13 \\ z &=5,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+2(5)=13\,⟹\,y=13-10=3.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=3$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(3)+2(5)=19\,⟹\,x=6.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=6,y=3$, and $z=5.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨6,3,5⟩.$

raw_source.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 8\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z &=-3 \\ y-2z &=-2 \\ z &=8,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=8$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-2(8)=-2\,⟹\,y=-2+16=14.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=14$ and $z=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(14)+(8)=-3\,⟹\,x=17.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=17,y=14$, and $z=8.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨17,14,8⟩.$

raw_source.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z &=6 \\ y+z &=5 \\ 2x+3y+2z &=14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z &=6 \\ y+z &=5 \\ z &=3,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=3$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(3)=5\,⟹\,y=5-3=2.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=2$ and $z=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(2)+(3)=6\,⟹\,x=6-5=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1,y=2$ and $z=3.$

Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=-3 \\ x+2y+2z &=2 \\ 3x+4y+4z &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 17\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=-3 \\ y &=5 \\ z &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=5$ and $z=-6$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+5+2(-6)=-3\,⟹\,x-7=-3\,⟹\,x=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4,$ $y=5,$ and $z=-6.$

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 3 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z &=1 \\ y-3z &=-9 \\ z &=1,\end{aligned}\right.

$$
y-3(1)=-9\,⟹\,y=-6.

x-(-6)+2(1)=1\,⟹\,x=-7.

raw_source.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=1 \\ 2x+3y+4z &=6 \\ 3x+3y+4z &=11\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & 3 & 4 & 11\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=1 \\ y &=4 \\ z &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=4$ and $z=-4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(4)+2(-4)=1\,⟹\,x=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5,y=4$, and $z=-4.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨5,4,-4⟩.$

raw_source.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -2 & 6 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 5 \\ -5 & -10 & 6 & -15\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
raw_source.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -2 & 6 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 5 \\ -5 & -10 & 6 & -15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 5 \\ -5 & -10 & 6 & -15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ -5 & -10 & 6 & -15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z &=3 \\ y+2z &=-4 \\ z &=0,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=0$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+2(0)=-4\,⟹\,y=-4.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-4$ and $z=0$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+2(-4)-(0)=3\,⟹\,x=11.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=11,y=-4$, and $z=0.$
